Break it into thirds. Start the first third truly easy, conversational pace, so you're not spending effort you'll need later. Settle into your normal easy pace for the middle, then run the last third the same or a touch stronger if you feel good.

Mentally, I'd chop it by landmarks instead of the full distance: run to a turnaround, then to a particular street, then a short push home. For longer efforts, walking for 30 to 60 seconds every mile or so is a smart tool, not a failure, especially on a hot day or when you're building toward a new distance.

Fuel and water matter once you're past an hour, so plan where you'll get them. Is this for a race, or are you building mileage?
